activity.title: Mock Interview Practice
activity.instructions: Read each interview question and type a response as if you were speaking to an employer. After each response, use the checklist to review your answer and identify one improvement.

scenarios.title: Opening Introduction
scenarios.context: You are interviewing for an entry-level position related to your major. The interviewer begins with a common opening question.
scenarios.question: Tell me about yourself.
response_tips: Keep the answer focused and organized.
Mention your academic background and one or two relevant experiences.
End by connecting your interest to the position.
sample_strong_elements: Clear interest in the employer or role

scenarios.title: Behavioral Question
scenarios.context: The employer wants to understand how you handle challenges in a team or academic setting.
scenarios.question: Tell me about a time you worked through a challenge with a team.
response_tips: Use the Situation, Task, Action, Result structure.
Focus on what you personally contributed.
Include what changed or what you learned.
sample_strong_elements: Clear action taken by the student

scenarios.title: Strengths
scenarios.context: The employer asks a direct question about what you would bring to the workplace.
scenarios.question: What is one strength you would bring to this role?
response_tips: Give an example that proves the strength.
Connect the strength to the position.

scenarios.title: Weaknesses
scenarios.context: The employer asks a question that can feel uncomfortable but is common in interviews.
scenarios.question: What is one area where you are currently working to improve?
response_tips: Choose a real but manageable improvement area.
Avoid naming a weakness that is essential to the role.
Explain the steps you are taking to improve.

scenarios.title: Work Authorization Conversation
scenarios.context: The employer asks about your ability to work in the United States. This module does not provide legal advice, but it helps you practice a clear and professional response.
scenarios.question: Will you now or in the future require sponsorship for employment authorization?
response_tips: Answer truthfully based on your current situation.
Keep the response concise and professional.
Avoid guessing about legal details if you are unsure.
Consult your campus international student office for accurate guidance about your visa status.
sample_strong_elements: Willingness to provide documentation through appropriate employer processes
scenarios.important_note: Visa and work authorization rules can change. Students should confirm their specific situation with their campus international student office or a qualified immigration professional.
